programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha ’ad uile air chrith leis an fhuachd air Planaid nan Clangairean – cho fuar ‘s gum b’ fheudar fiù 's dhan Chearc Iarainn dèanamh air Uamh nan Clangairean 'son cumail blàth. Nach math g’ eil Granaidh comasach is taiceil san t-suidheachadh seo! Everyone is shivering with the cold on the Planet, so cold that even the Iron Chicken has had to go to the cave to get warm. Fortunately, Granny proves to be helpful.

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Tha Linda a’ tadhal air a caraidean Meaban is Moo gus innse dhaibh mu chuirm a chunnaic i. Tha seo gam brosnachadh gus cuirm shònraichte a chur air dòigh dhithse agus, às dèidh beagan ullachaidh, tha iad deiseil airson a thoirt chun an àrd-ùrlair. Linda visits her friend Meaban and Moo to tell them about her trip to the theatre. This gives them the idea to put on a concert for Linda and the stage is soon set for a very special performance!

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona and Baba plan a surprise for Mama and Papa - they're going to collect some lovely bright flowers for them! Baba comes across a honeybee in the meadow. Wherever bees are, there'll be flowers - they know where the best ones are! Oona, Baba and the bees find lots of beautiful flowers, but when they get to the Undergrowth, the Pufflings see more bees than they bargained for. Tha Oona is Baba ag ullachadh iongnadh 'son Mamaidh is Papaidh – 'ad a' dol a bhuain lusan breàgha, daiteach air an son! Tha Baba a' faicinn seillean-meala san achadh. Ge brith cà' bheil seilleanan, bidh lusan – fhios aca far a bheil an fheadhainn as fheàrr! Tha Oona, Baba agus na seilleanan a' lorg tòrr lusan àlainn, ach nuiar a ruigeas 'ad am Preaslach, tha na buthaidean a' faicinn barrachd sheilleanan na bha iad an dùil.

programme.title: Creag nam Buthaidean/Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Baba can't wait for his swimming lesson, and he has a great instructor - his big sister Oona. She teaches Baba to paddle, steer with his feet, and put his head under the water. With some practice, and encouragement from Oona and Mama, Baba starts to get the hang of it - but diving proves much more difficult, until Lala drops a shiny shell in the water. Tha fadachd air Baba 'son an leasan snàimh aige, agus tha tidsear air leth aige – a phiuthar mhòr, Oona. Tha Oona a' teagasg grunnachadh do Bhaba, stiùireadh le spògan, agus a bhith a' cur a cheann fon uisge. Le beagan ullachaidh, 's le brosnachadh bho Oona is Mamaidh, tha Baba a' teannadh ri làmh an uachdair fhaighinn air cùisean – ach tha daibheadh fada nas dorra...gus an leag Lala slige dhealrach dhan uisge.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.desc: Bidh Latha na Cloinne ann a dh’aithghearr agus tha Peicein is a charaidean a’ cur romhpa tuairmsean a thoirt dham pàrantan a thaobh na preusantan a tha iad ag iarraidh. Ged nach eil iad a’ faighinn na bha iad ag iarraidh, tha iad ag iomlaid nam preusantan aca le chèile, is aig deireadh an latha tha iad a’ faighinn na bha iad ag iarraidh. Children’s Day is approaching, and Petit and his friends decide they will give their parents clues on what gifts they want. Even though the youngsters don't receive their exact wishes, they end up exchanging presents to get what they all wanted.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc: 'S toigh le na h-Abadas a bhith cluich falach-fead. Tha am facal ùr cuideachd comasach air rudan a lorg nuair nach urrainn am faicinn. Dè th'ann agus cò an Abadas a b'fheàrr airson am facal a lorg? The Abadas love playing hide-and-seek. The day's word is also able to seek out things that can't be seen. What could it be and which Abada would be the best one to go and look for the word?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Kim Carnie a’ leughadh Cia mheud cadal gu mo cho-là-breith? Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Amber Stewart agus a dhealbhachadh le Layn Marlow. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Dòmhnall Iain MacLeòid. A bedtime story for young children. Kim Carnie reads Cia mheud cadal gu mo cho-là-breith?, written by Amber Stewart, illustrated by Layn Marlow and translated into Gaelic by Donald John MacLeod.

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Tha Stella air a glacadh eadar Mia is Freya nuair a tha ‘ad ag argamaid. Ciamar a gheibh i fuasgladh air an trod gus am bi ‘ad air ais nan caraidean a-rithist Stella is caught between Mia and Freya when they argue. How will she find a solution to the fighting so that they will be friends again?

programme.title: An Teaghlach Rìoghail an Ath-dhoras/The Royal Next Door
programme.desc: Nuair tha Stella a’ coinneachadh ris an sgoilear iomlaid aice, Orla, chan eil cùisean a' dol cho math 's a bha i an dùil. Tha Orla caran nèonach. Ciamar a gheibh Stella ceangal eatarra gus am faigh iad air adhart le chèile? When Stella meets her exchange student, Orla, things don’t go as well as she’d hoped. Orla is a little strange. How will Stella find some kind of common bond so that they will get on well with each other?

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: Nuair a tha Hikari ‘son rìs fhàs, tha Mgr. Yamanaka, fear a th' air a bhith na thuathanach rìs còrr is caogad bliadhna, dha comhairleachadh. Tha a’ chùis a’ còrdadh rithe ’s tha i a co-dhùnadh gum bi i na tuathanach rìs nuair a dh' fhàsas i mòr. When Hikari wants to grow rice, she gets advice from Mr Yamanaka, who’s been a rice farmer for over 50 years. The process is so enjoyable that Hikari decides she wants to be a rice farmer when she grows up.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Tha Sebastian dol a theagasg an clas an-diugh air a’ bheinn ‘s tha e dol a dhearbhadh gu bheil e cho eòlach air na beanntan ‘s nach eil feum air a dhol dhan sgoil. Today’s class is going to be taught by Sebastian on the mountain and he is going to prove that his knowledge is so vast that he doesn’t need to go to school.

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an Treud a' cluinntinn bhana nan reòiteagan air fàire agus a' tighinn an àrd le plana faighinn thuice. Leis an dràibhear a' faighinn cuideachadh, tha na caoraich air an dòigh le reòiteagan gun chrìoch - ach saoil am faigh daoine a-mach dè rinn iad? The flock hear the enticing tunes of an ice cream van approaching and quickly hatch a plan to divert it into their field. While the driver seeks help, the flock have great fun with an endless supply of ice cream. But will they be able to cover their tracks before they're discovered?

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Scottish Women's Premier League (BBC ALBA)
programme.desc: Playoff SWPL beò air BBC ALBA le Obar Dheathain a’ dol an aghaidh Queen’s Park. An geama slàn ri fhaicinn le aithris bho Donna NicNèill. Live SWPL playoff action as Aberdeen take on Queen’s Park. Full live coverage with commentary from Donna MacNeill.

programme.title: Jimmy Johnstone
programme.desc: Deich bliadhna às dèidh a bhàs, tha 'Jimmy Johnstone' a' dèanamh luaidh air beatha fear dheth na sàr thàlantan ann an eachdraidh spòrs na h-Alba, ag innse soirbheas is doilgheas cluicheadair ball-coise sònraichte nach tèid à cuimhne gu bràth, laoch aig sgioba Celtic, cèile agus athair a chaill a bheatha air sàilleabh tinneas motor neurone aig aois 61. This programme examines the life of a phenomenal Scottish sporting talent Jimmy Johnstone, telling the story of the highs and the lows of an unforgettable working class footballer, Celtic legend, husband and father who lost his life to motor neurone disease age 61.

programme.title: Brunch le Abigail
programme.desc: ’S e Lite am bracaist as fheàrr le Abigail airson a thoirt air falbh. Ach chan eil càil sìmplidh mun dòigh a th’ aicese air a dhèanamh. Tha i ga lìonadh le Ùbhlan, Caineal agus Siorap Mhaplais, agus e a’ cur Crumbail Ùbhlan na cuimhne. Abigail’s favourite takeaway breakfast is porridge. Her version is no simple dish, though, and contains apples, cinnamon and maple syrup to remind her of apple crumble. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Belladrum
programme.desc: Tha Fiona NicChoinnich agus Niall Iain Dòmhnallach a’ cur fàilt’ air Toby Lee gu Àrd-Ùrlar Hot House aig Belladrum 2025. Ged nach eil Toby ach 20 bliadhna a dh’aois, tha na sàr-sgilean cluiche agus a ghuth iongantach air cothroman fhuasgladh dha air an àrd-ùrlar leis an luchd-ciùil as fheàrr – mar Buddy Guy, Billy Gibbons, Peter Frampton, Slash agus Joe Bonamassa. Fiona MacKenzie and Niall Iain Macdonald welcome Toby Lee to the Hot House Stage at Belladrum. A mind-blowing guitarist and a voice to match, the 20-year-old’s music belies his age and has seen him sharing the stage with the best in the business, including Buddy Guy, Billy Gibbons, Peter Frampton, Slash and Joe Bonamassa.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: The Prince, the Showgirl and Me
programme.desc: Documentary. Sir Laurence Olivier's personal assistant Colin Cark reveals the trials that beset The Prince and the Showgirl film with Marilyn Monroe.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take players so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. A team of three lads from the Cambridge Quiz Society pit their wits against a trio of Oxford Librarians with specialisms as diverse as Comparative Slavonic Linguistics, Classics and Theology. They compete to draw together the connections between things which, at first glance, seem utterly random, from Goldeneye to The Kilns to Hill Top to Haworth Parsonage.

programme.title: Art of Scandinavia

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc: John Peel and Janice Long present this pop chart programme, first broadcast on 29 May 1986. Featuring Doctor and the Medics, Robert Palmer, The Real Thing, Tears for Fears, Pete Wylie, Spitting Image and Peter Gabriel.

programme.title: Miles Davis: Birth of the Cool
programme.desc: Miles Davis - horn player, bandleader, innovator. Elegant, intellectual, vain. Callous, conflicted, controversial. Magnificent, mercurial. Genius. The very embodiment of cool. The man with a sound so beautiful it could break your heart. The central theme of Miles Davis's life was his restless determination to break boundaries and live life on his own terms. It made him a star. It also made him incredibly difficult to live with for the people who loved him most. Again and again, in music and in life, Miles broke with convention - and when he thought his work came to represent a new convention, he changed it again. Miles's bold disregard for tradition, his clarity of vision, his relentless drive and constant thirst for new experiences made him an inspiring collaborator to fellow musicians and a cultural icon to generations of listeners. It made him an innovator in music - from bebop to cool jazz, modern quintets, orchestral music, jazz fusion, rock ‘n’ roll and even hip-hop. Featuring never-before-seen archival footage, studio outtakes and rare photos, this film tells the story of a truly singular talent and unpacks the music and the myth of the man behind the horn.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Alan Yentob shares the fascinating story of how the 1974 broadcast of the great Ella Fitzgerald singing in Ronnie Scott’s nightclub came about. In a tale of tenacity combined with new camera technology, Alan recounts how, as a young TV producer, he managed to persuade Ella’s manager to let the BBC film Ella in full flight at London’s home of jazz, capturing forever what is now considered to be a performance of true musical significance.

programme.title: Ella Fitzgerald's Other Show
programme.desc: Ella Fitzgerald in performance at Ronnie Scott's Jazz Club in 1974.

programme.title: Cleo Laine at the BBC
programme.desc: A special celebration of Britain’s First Lady of Jazz’s finest moments on the BBC to coincide with her 95th birthday. Cleo Laine became a star after joining The John Dankworth Seven in the 1950s. Internationally renowned for her mastery of the ‘scat’ singing style, and with a voice that has been described as ‘one of the richest contraltos in recording history’, Cleo has now enjoyed over six decades of success and acclaim here and across the world. These are the highlights of her extraordinary career, with classic songs like Send in the Clowns and I Love You, Porgy, and duets with John Williams, Dudley Moore, Tony Bennett, and of course, her musical partner and fellow jazz legend Johnny Dankworth.

programme.title: Jazz 625 at the BBC
programme.desc: Programme celebrating the archive of this legendary BBC jazz concert show from the mid 1960s, so titled because the newly launched BBC 2 was broadcasting on 625-UHF lines (the HD of the time) unlike the 405-VHF of BBC 1 and ITV. It features classic performances from legends such as Duke Ellington, Dave Brubeck and Dizzy Gillespie and The Julian 'Cannonball' Adderley Sextet, alongside rarely seen sessions from the likes of Wes Montgomery, Marian McPartland, Chris Barber's Jazz Band and Willie 'The Lion' Smith.

programme.title: The Prince, the Showgirl and Me
programme.desc: Documentary. Sir Laurence Olivier's personal assistant Colin Cark reveals the trials that beset The Prince and the Showgirl film with Marilyn Monroe.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take players so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. A team of three lads from the Cambridge Quiz Society pit their wits against a trio of Oxford Librarians with specialisms as diverse as Comparative Slavonic Linguistics, Classics and Theology. They compete to draw together the connections between things which, at first glance, seem utterly random, from Goldeneye to The Kilns to Hill Top to Haworth Parsonage.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin meets a big fan of the show in Hampshire but is disappointed to hear he’s ignored the golden rules of buying at auction. In Kent, we see the conclusion of a period restoration that Jacqui first saw in early 2023. Dion’s taking in the scenery in beautiful north Wales.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents as a team of celebrity sport stars - former England rugby player Ugo Monye, tennis supremo Judy Murray, goalkeeper David James and Scottish football legend Pat Nevin - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents as a team of celebrity sport stars - former England rugby player Ugo Monye, tennis supremo Judy Murray, goalkeeper David James and Scottish football legend Pat Nevin - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents as a team of celebrity sport stars - former England rugby player Ugo Monye, tennis supremo Judy Murray, goalkeeper David James and Scottish football legend Pat Nevin - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: A man whose home address is hijacked by a fraudster using the name Michael Jackson receives traffic fines and a visit from a bailiff but says the authorities won’t help. Also on the programme, how a leading airline’s loyalty points scheme is being targeted by thieves.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin meets a big fan of the show in Hampshire but is disappointed to hear he’s ignored the golden rules of buying at auction. In Kent, we see the conclusion of a period restoration that Jacqui first saw in early 2023. Dion’s taking in the scenery in beautiful north Wales.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: The Oakley winery 'family' is shaken by a tremor and strained relationships. Daisy is stressed, Louis is leaving, while Nic and Vic make a request. Return of the earthy New Zealand comedy drama.

programme.title: Under the Vines

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Now that her sons have fledged the nest, today’s buyer wants a new lease of life in a rural home that has business potential. She’s set her sights on either Devon or Dorset, where Briony May Williams has some wonderful property options to show her. Briony also meets another entrepreneurial couple who’ve converted an old railway carriage into a fine dining destination.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents as a team of celebrity sport stars - former England rugby player Ugo Monye, tennis supremo Judy Murray, goalkeeper David James and Scottish football legend Pat Nevin - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents as a team of celebrity sport stars - former England rugby player Ugo Monye, tennis supremo Judy Murray, goalkeeper David James and Scottish football legend Pat Nevin - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

Can she capture the warmth, loss and love bound up in Sandra’s most precious place?

programme.desc: Martin meets a big fan of the show in Hampshire but is disappointed to hear he’s ignored the golden rules of buying at auction. In Kent, we see the conclusion of a period restoration that Jacqui first saw in early 2023. Dion’s taking in the scenery in beautiful north Wales.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Under the Vines

programme.title: Under the Vines
programme.desc: Nic suffers distress on a hike, but Dr David helps and heartens Daisy. Gus and Griffin brave Morag’s guesthouse. Struck-off Louis gets legal.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: Now that her sons have fledged the nest, today’s buyer wants a new lease of life in a rural home that has business potential. She’s set her sights on either Devon or Dorset, where Briony May Williams has some wonderful property options to show her. Briony also meets another entrepreneurial couple who’ve converted an old railway carriage into a fine dining destination.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents as a team of celebrity sport stars - former England rugby player Ugo Monye, tennis supremo Judy Murray, goalkeeper David James and Scottish football legend Pat Nevin - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.desc: Martin meets a big fan of the show in Hampshire but is disappointed to hear he’s ignored the golden rules of buying at auction. In Kent, we see the conclusion of a period restoration that Jacqui first saw in early 2023. Dion’s taking in the scenery in beautiful north Wales.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion visits a pub frozen in time, where last orders were called in the 1960s and everything was left untouched. In the Devon town of Buckfastleigh, the Valiant Soldier was an inn for more than two centuries and is now a museum, giving visitors a glimpse into the past. Inside the recreated interior, Christina is told about the pub’s redoubtable landlady and the custom back in the 60s of refusing service to women in the bar. In Hele, near Exeter, two teams of shoppers rush around an antiques centre with their experts, hoping to bag profitable bargains. On the red team are dad and daughter Ade and Mel, helped by Ben Cooper, and for the blues, it’s friends Martin and Mark, aided by Gary Pe. With 60 minutes on the clock, the blue team’s first stop is a shining suit of armour. Across the centre, Mel gazes into a £200 crystal ball – does it foretell a win for the reds? In Chippenham, auctioneer Tim Weeks confidently predicts a few profits for the teams, but who will go home the victor?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents as a team of celebrity sport stars - former England rugby player Ugo Monye, tennis supremo Judy Murray, goalkeeper David James and Scottish football legend Pat Nevin - take on the Bridge of Lies for their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie, and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. programme.title: Away with the Tartan Army - Scotland’s Best Moments
programme.desc: Stuart Cosgrove and Tam Cowan explore the highs and lows of following the Scotland international men’s team and take a trip with the Tartan Army to countdown ten of Scotland’s best moments. Featuring a trip to Sweden for Scotland’s first Euros in 1992, the opening match of the 1998 World Cup in France against holders Brazil, and an emotional visit to a war-ravaged Bosnia in 1999 on a mission of peace. These are just some of the amazing moments experienced by the faithful Scotland support, known the world over as the Tartan Army. These colourful, friendly supporters follow Scotland to the ends of the earth, win, lose or draw, and they have witnessed Scotland moments that will live on in the memory forever. What will the top moment be? Leigh Griffiths’ two free kicks against England at Hampden in 2017? The famous win at Wembley in 1977? James McFadden’s goal against France in 2007? Find out as Stuart and Tam introduce Scotland’s emotional highs and lows as seen through the eyes of the Tartan Army, and ranked by a specially chosen group of journalists, pundits and former players.

programme.title: Two Doors Down
programme.desc: Beth and Cathy think they are doing their good deed for the day when they drop Christine off at the hospital reception, but while Cathy manages to slip away, poor Beth doesn't get off so lightly and is committed to a visit post-op. With a long list of demands from Christine, Beth and Eric return later with her supplies to find that instead of being sore and exhausted after surgery, she has been sleeping off her dinner. It emerges the operation has been postponed until the following morning. As nurse Heather weathers Christine's demands, Colin arrives followed by Michelle and Alan. The ensuing group discussion leaves Christine very worried about her chances of survival.

programme.title: A Good Girl's Guide to Murder
programme.desc: After solving the Andie Bell case, Pip is forced to confront the consequences of what her investigation exposed. It may have cleared Sal’s name, but it tore Cara’s family apart, and the guilt weighs heavily on Pip. In an attempt to rebuild her relationship with Cara, Pip releases a podcast to tell the world the real story. The only person yet to face justice is Max Hastings, and as his trial approaches, Pip is determined to help his victims find closure. However, the prosecution’s case begins to falter when Becca Bell withdraws from testifying. Unwilling to accept this, Pip musters the courage to visit Becca in prison with the hope of convincing her that giving evidence still matters. Pip wants to focus on supporting Ravi at the upcoming memorial for his brother, but when a mysterious note promising information on Max appears in her locker, Pip must make a difficult decision. Little Kilton comes together to say goodbye to both Andie Bell and Sal Singh. The end of one dark chapter gives way to another, as Cara finds herself in a dangerous situation, and Jamie Reynolds, Connor’s brother and a key witness in Max’s trial, disappears without warning.

programme.desc: Alan and the final five designers head to Leeds to transform studio rental apartments. They must cleverly divide open-plan spaces and inject character into show apartments to entice potential renters. Former Interior Design Masters winner Lynsey Ford joins Michelle to critique the designs, and they are blown away by the dramatically different results.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Stephen joins response officers Anna and Perri as they attend a 999 call made from a property in Belfast. A man has had bleach squirted directly on his face and into his eyes during a domestic dispute. At risk to their own safety, the officers enter the property to find the suspect upstairs, reportedly self-harming. There are reports he has strangled a dog. Across town, Tom and Nigel race to the scene of a serious crash that has left a pedestrian badly injured. As soon as they arrive, a scared and tearful woman approaches. She thinks the man lying in the middle of the road, being worked on by paramedics, is her partner. It’s down to Tom to deliver a message the woman will never forget. Later, adrenaline levels spike as Stephen and the team race to reports of an angry crowd surrounding the home of a convicted sex offender. As the tension rises, Stephen engages with the increasingly irate crowd, while Nigel formulates a plan to get the sex offender out of his house to safety.

programme.title: Two Weeks in August
programme.desc: Zoe and her family arrive on a remote Greek island, hoping a holiday reunion with friends will be an escape from reality. But can she keep pretending when her husband Dan’s dark secret threatens to ruin everything? A hedonistic first night party is the release they all need. But it sets off a chain of events that will change them all forever. Zoe begins to wonder if there are bigger forces at play. We are in Greece, after all, land of the gods.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion’s in Sheffield, where he feels there is scope to double the size of a property. He is also in Nottingham with layout changes on the menu. Jacqui offers a 16th-century history lesson in Windsor.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his travels in Budapest, Michael Portillo begins in the small town of Huvösvölgy, in the hills above the city, at a surprising railway run almost entirely by children, dating back to the communist era. All of the staff, except for the train drivers, are volunteers aged ten to 14. Back in the city, he visits the former home of Béla Bartók, one of Hungary’s most famous pianists and composers, and learns how the country’s folk music inspired his work. Next, Michael heads across the Danube to the headquarters of the low-cost airline Wizz Air, one of the country’s post-communist success stories. At the pilot academy, he endures a stressful emergency landing and tries his hand at flying a plane.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From scandalous society portraits to glittering royal furniture and the restoration of lost landscapes, this episode reveals how the legacy of the Grand Tour continues to shape Britain’s great houses – and the work being done today to protect their remarkable stories for the future.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Ben Fogle presents an appeal on behalf of Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, a charity that provides support as well as trained assistance dogs to help those living with deafness or hearing loss in the UK.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are the British Industrial Revolution, the films of Christopher Guest, Charles Rennie Mackintosh and Succession.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: The county of Yorkshire is the setting for Christine Walkden's balloon tour of Britain. At Scampston Hall we discover two superstar garden designers and meet young gardener Nathan, who is just starting out. At York Gate Garden, Christine catches up with an old friend and we discover the Yorkshireman who was the father of aviation.

programme.title: The Secret Life of Elephants
programme.desc: After the drought, the rains have arrived, but has baby elephant Breeze survived? As hundreds of elephants descend on the reserve for the breeding season, the research team hit their busiest time of year. With the help of new technology, Saba Douglas-Hamilton tracks down the biggest land animals on earth - the mighty bull elephants. But even Saba is keeping her distance when Rommel, a dangerous bull who once flattened a car and tried to kill two of the team's researchers, arrives on the scene. Outside the reserve, there is a shocking development when Onesmas Kahindi investigates two mysterious deaths - could poachers be targeting the local elephants? When field researcher David Daballen finds a baby elephant in desperate trouble, he and the team must mount a life-or-death operation to save her.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the experts visit Chichester Cathedral. Finds include a fine cow creamer, a rare 18th-century games purse and a valuable necklace which was found in an attic.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Crowcombe Court in West Somerset. The grand house was built in 1739 as a statement of wealth and a place to entertain. Antiques experts James Lewis and Thomas Plant uncover some promotional sausage plates that were designed to promote the wares of an exuberant Victorian butcher. Paul also rides on the footplate of a steam locomotive on West Somerset Railway.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Before boarding his train at Budapest’s historic Nyugati station, Michael Portillo explores its sumptuous royal waiting room, built specially for the Austro-Hungarian emperor Franz Joseph I and his empress, Elizabeth. Heading south, his next destination is the country’s third city of Szeged, close to the Serbian and Romanian borders. In the city’s historic centre, he finds the magnificent Great Synagogue, built in 1902, which reflects the size and prominence of Szeged’s Jewish population at that time. Just outside the city, on the banks of the River Tisza, Michael visits a region known for producing Hungary’s favourite spice, paprika, from ground red peppers. At a fourth-generation family farm, he tries a freshly picked pepper and joins the family for a hearty paprika stew.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: The wait is over: the search for Northern Ireland’s greatest garden is almost at an end. Five passionate gardeners have reached the final. After an early autumn road trip spent revisiting these five truly incredible gardens to refresh their memories, Carol and Diarmuid join the finalists, their families and friends at Greenmount’s walled garden in County Antrim to reveal which one of the five will be named greatest garden.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Some more unusual methods of growing are demonstrated at Beechgrove Garden. Ruth Vichos attempts to produce a mushroom crop and there’s a report on some of Scotland’s best bonsai, with everything you need to know to start that form of cultivation. Brian Cunningham is in the Seaside Garden at Beechgrove refreshing the planting with varieties that can withstand a coastal climate and Brian turns conifers into sculptures with topiary. Plus the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With summer just around the corner, Monty is bringing bold colour to the garden, planting gingers and cannas, setting out tomatoes and sowing wallflowers straight into the soil. From her Devon garden, Carol Klein is exploring the latest plant science, uncovering what is really going on inside a seed the moment it is sown, and how this pioneering knowledge can transform the way people garden. Rekha Mistry is also on a mission to grow big in a small space, using only pots on her patio. In Oxfordshire, a garden designed for both beauty and biodiversity shows how plants can support wildlife as well as people. And a viewer in rural France shares a breathtaking, naturalistic plot that blends seamlessly with the surrounding landscape.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a windswept island chapel battered by the North Sea to a quiet Welsh farmhouse that shaped the future of a language, this episode travels to two remote National Trust sites whose powerful stories have inspired centuries of pilgrims, revealing the delicate conservation work protecting their remarkable stories.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul, Bob and Ted travel a short distance to Thornwood Springs Fishery in Essex, a complex of three lakes on the edges of Epping Forest, in search of a big rudd - although there's also the chance of a trout in the waters. Later, they pull up at a churchyard, and Bob reveals they are ‘champing’ – camping overnight in a church, in this case St Nicholas’s in the village of Berden.

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Lucy Hockings.

programme.title: Love & Mercy
programme.desc: Biographical drama. At the height of success with his band The Beach Boys, musical genius Brian Wilson begins to suffer from mental illness, which is not helped by his experiments with LSD. A decade later, Wilson is in the grip of shady psychotherapist Eugene Landy, whose extreme treatment is causing further deterioration, until the day he decides he wants a new car.

A decade later, Wilson is in the grip of shady psychotherapist Eugene Landy, whose extreme treatment is causing further deterioration, until the day he decides he wants a new car.

programme.title: MasterChef
programme.desc: Knockout week is coming to an end, but not before a few more cooks have to say goodbye. Ten contestants remain, and there is only room in the semi-finals for eight.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: Alan and the final five designers head to Leeds to transform studio rental apartments. They must cleverly divide open-plan spaces and inject character into show apartments to entice potential renters. Former Interior Design Masters winner Lynsey Ford joins Michelle to critique the designs, and they are blown away by the dramatically different results.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Stephen joins response officers Anna and Perri as they attend a 999 call made from a property in Belfast. A man has had bleach squirted directly on his face and into his eyes during a domestic dispute. At risk to their own safety, the officers enter the property to find the suspect upstairs, reportedly self-harming. There are reports he has strangled a dog. Across town, Tom and Nigel race to the scene of a serious crash that has left a pedestrian badly injured. As soon as they arrive, a scared and tearful woman approaches. She thinks the man lying in the middle of the road, being worked on by paramedics, is her partner. It’s down to Tom to deliver a message the woman will never forget. Later, adrenaline levels spike as Stephen and the team race to reports of an angry crowd surrounding the home of a convicted sex offender. As the tension rises, Stephen engages with the increasingly irate crowd, while Nigel formulates a plan to get the sex offender out of his house to safety.

programme.title: Two Weeks in August
programme.desc: Zoe and her family arrive on a remote Greek island, hoping a holiday reunion with friends will be an escape from reality. But can she keep pretending when her husband Dan’s dark secret threatens to ruin everything? A hedonistic first night party is the release they all need. But it sets off a chain of events that will change them all forever. Zoe begins to wonder if there are bigger forces at play. We are in Greece, after all, land of the gods.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Dion’s in Sheffield, where he feels there is scope to double the size of a property. He is also in Nottingham with layout changes on the menu. Jacqui offers a 16th-century history lesson in Windsor.

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Continuing his travels in Budapest, Michael Portillo begins in the small town of Huvösvölgy, in the hills above the city, at a surprising railway run almost entirely by children, dating back to the communist era. All of the staff, except for the train drivers, are volunteers aged ten to 14. Back in the city, he visits the former home of Béla Bartók, one of Hungary’s most famous pianists and composers, and learns how the country’s folk music inspired his work. Next, Michael heads across the Danube to the headquarters of the low-cost airline Wizz Air, one of the country’s post-communist success stories. At the pilot academy, he endures a stressful emergency landing and tries his hand at flying a plane.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From scandalous society portraits to glittering royal furniture and the restoration of lost landscapes, this episode reveals how the legacy of the Grand Tour continues to shape Britain’s great houses – and the work being done today to protect their remarkable stories for the future.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson
programme.desc: Nick Robinson in conversation with people who influence our political thinking.

programme.title: Lifeline
programme.desc: Ben Fogle presents an appeal on behalf of Hearing Dogs for Deaf People, a charity that provides support as well as trained assistance dogs to help those living with deafness or hearing loss in the UK.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: The unique quiz show where if a player gives an Impossible answer, they are immediately eliminated. Which of the 24 contestants will face the £10,000 question today?

programme.title: Mastermind
programme.desc: Clive Myrie presents another heat of the classic quiz where contenders take on the famous black chair under the glare of the spotlight and the ticking clock in an attempt to become the next Mastermind champion. The specialist subjects are the British Industrial Revolution, the films of Christopher Guest, Charles Rennie Mackintosh and Succession.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Glorious Gardens from Above
programme.desc: The county of Yorkshire is the setting for Christine Walkden's balloon tour of Britain. At Scampston Hall we discover two superstar garden designers and meet young gardener Nathan, who is just starting out. At York Gate Garden, Christine catches up with an old friend and we discover the Yorkshireman who was the father of aviation.

programme.title: The Secret Life of Elephants
programme.desc: After the drought, the rains have arrived, but has baby elephant Breeze survived? As hundreds of elephants descend on the reserve for the breeding season, the research team hit their busiest time of year. With the help of new technology, Saba Douglas-Hamilton tracks down the biggest land animals on earth - the mighty bull elephants. But even Saba is keeping her distance when Rommel, a dangerous bull who once flattened a car and tried to kill two of the team's researchers, arrives on the scene. Outside the reserve, there is a shocking development when Onesmas Kahindi investigates two mysterious deaths - could poachers be targeting the local elephants? When field researcher David Daballen finds a baby elephant in desperate trouble, he and the team must mount a life-or-death operation to save her.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and the experts visit Chichester Cathedral. Finds include a fine cow creamer, a rare 18th-century games purse and a valuable necklace which was found in an attic.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Paul Martin presents from Crowcombe Court in West Somerset. The grand house was built in 1739 as a statement of wealth and a place to entertain. Antiques experts James Lewis and Thomas Plant uncover some promotional sausage plates that were designed to promote the wares of an exuberant Victorian butcher. Paul also rides on the footplate of a steam locomotive on West Somerset Railway.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Cheryl Baker, Chris Bavin, Axel Blake and Sophie Willan take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Continental Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Before boarding his train at Budapest’s historic Nyugati station, Michael Portillo explores its sumptuous royal waiting room, built specially for the Austro-Hungarian emperor Franz Joseph I and his empress, Elizabeth. Heading south, his next destination is the country’s third city of Szeged, close to the Serbian and Romanian borders. In the city’s historic centre, he finds the magnificent Great Synagogue, built in 1902, which reflects the size and prominence of Szeged’s Jewish population at that time. Just outside the city, on the banks of the River Tisza, Michael visits a region known for producing Hungary’s favourite spice, paprika, from ground red peppers. At a fourth-generation family farm, he tries a freshly picked pepper and joins the family for a hearty paprika stew.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein
programme.desc: The wait is over: the search for Northern Ireland’s greatest garden is almost at an end. Five passionate gardeners have reached the final. After an early autumn road trip spent revisiting these five truly incredible gardens to refresh their memories, Carol and Diarmuid join the finalists, their families and friends at Greenmount’s walled garden in County Antrim to reveal which one of the five will be named greatest garden.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: Some more unusual methods of growing are demonstrated at Beechgrove Garden. Ruth Vichos attempts to produce a mushroom crop and there’s a report on some of Scotland’s best bonsai, with everything you need to know to start that form of cultivation. Brian Cunningham is in the Seaside Garden at Beechgrove refreshing the planting with varieties that can withstand a coastal climate and Brian turns conifers into sculptures with topiary. Plus the week’s handy hints.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: With summer just around the corner, Monty is bringing bold colour to the garden, planting gingers and cannas, setting out tomatoes and sowing wallflowers straight into the soil. From her Devon garden, Carol Klein is exploring the latest plant science, uncovering what is really going on inside a seed the moment it is sown, and how this pioneering knowledge can transform the way people garden. Rekha Mistry is also on a mission to grow big in a small space, using only pots on her patio. In Oxfordshire, a garden designed for both beauty and biodiversity shows how plants can support wildlife as well as people. And a viewer in rural France shares a breathtaking, naturalistic plot that blends seamlessly with the surrounding landscape.

programme.title: Hidden Treasures of the National Trust
programme.desc: From a windswept island chapel battered by the North Sea to a quiet Welsh farmhouse that shaped the future of a language, this episode travels to two remote National Trust sites whose powerful stories have inspired centuries of pilgrims, revealing the delicate conservation work protecting their remarkable stories.

programme.title: Mortimer & Whitehouse: Gone Fishing
programme.desc: Paul, Bob and Ted travel a short distance to Thornwood Springs Fishery in Essex, a complex of three lakes on the edges of Epping Forest, in search of a big rudd - although there's also the chance of a trout in the waters. Later, they pull up at a churchyard, and Bob reveals they are ‘champing’ – camping overnight in a church, in this case St Nicholas’s in the village of Berden.

programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day. With Lucy Hockings.

Thank goodness Duggee is so wise!

programme.title: Lu & the Bally Bunch

The Very Important Lady visits the boat and falls apart. Her head rolls back and forth throughout the boat, disrupting the Twirlywoos' efforts to put her body back together.

programme.title: Something Special

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: Preschool series. Tinky Winky finds a party invitation and shows it to Dipsy, Laa-Laa and Po. The invitation takes flight, and the Teletubbies follow it to find a Tiddlytubbies' party.

programme.desc: Nigel and Baby Bear welcome babies Noah, Baani, Zachary, Amber, Amelia, Jace, Hunter and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Parents, carers and their babies at home are invited to join in with all the fun activities too! Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are toy animals which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate toy animals inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular rhyme ’Hickory Dickory Dock’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: Lisa and the children paint calming mobiles, learning British Sign Language signs for mama, buy and cry, then sing and sign Hush Little Baby Don’t You Cry.

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: Rebecca washes all the hats, ready for a silly hat party - but Murphi’s special party hat has shrunk. Although he’s disappointed, it gives Murphi an idea - a clothes peg giraffe. The Mini Monsters are using everyday things to create great makes, and a call comes in on the Magic Monster Mirror from Rebecca’s aunt. Murphi’s mega monster make is a fun woolly head game inspired by scraps of wool delivered by the Recycling Express.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Minty soars over the valley on a baby Bokchoydactyl's back.

programme.title: Bluey

Duggee is quick to explain to the Squirrels that there is no right or wrong way to play and that everyone is different. They go on a journey with the ball, watching it bounce, roll and slide from ear to paw as it rebounds between animals. The ball gets hit with a racket, flies through the sky, falls from a cliff and floats in the sea.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: It’s Mummy’s birthday! Henry, Sophie and Mama go on a secret shopping trip to find the perfect present. Back at home, Henry plans out a treasure map and sends Mummy on a heroic birthday adventure. Can she brave the hot lava? And will she find her presents?

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Vinnie's family is English and they come from a city called Bristol, which is located in the west of England. Bristol is famous for hot-air balloons and pirates! Vinnie makes his tarts by mixing the leaves from parsley and thyme into cream cheese. Then, he makes rectangles out of pastry and spreads the cream cheese mixture on top. To finish off his recipe, Vinnie lays chopped asparagus on top of the cream cheese, before it goes in the oven to cook. Vinnie's special ingredient is asparagus. Do you think his friends will like it in his tarts? With his meal, Vinnie also has a brilliant pirate-themed party planned for his friends. Arrr!

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today’s episode it’s playtime! Maddie is finding out about wind-up toys and how they move along. We see inside a wind-up truck and Maddie uses her special cameras to show us how the spring inside gets tighter and tighter and stores energy so that when it is released the cogs inside move the wheels. Next, Maddie visits a factory where cricket bats are made from willow trees, because it’s bouncy and strong. First the tree trunk is cut using a chainsaw and we learn how the wood is shaped using lots of different cutting and sanding machines. We see inside a robot that is shaped like a pineapple! Maddie uses her special slow-motion camera to see all the wood shavings flying off as the bat takes shape.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Rayane, Karim and Luca are having a sleepover, when hearing dog Diesel is woken in the middle of the night by a strange hissing noise. Is there a slithery snake in the kitchen?

The pair feed this cute character his breakfast. Next, they meet a pair of aardvarks, Terry and Dobby. These two terrific diggers use their super long tongues to lap up their lunch. Hippos and aardvarks are very different, but Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the unusual and extraordinary wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.desc: Waffle, Jess, Gramps and Angela help Pepper find a new owner by making a leaflet. Waffle tries to help Mrs Hobbs, too, but causes chaos. Waffle hopes Mrs Hobbs will adopt Pepper.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Bernie rides to the rescue – on a turtle taxi!

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: Two-part documentary series examining the years between 1977 and 1984 when three English football clubs - Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa - lifted the European Cup a record seven times. Featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers the break-up of Brian Clough's hugely successful Nottingham Forest, the re-emergence of Liverpool - who lifted their third and fourth European Cups in 1981 and 1984 - and the incredible story of Aston Villa, who upset all the odds to claim their one and only win in the competition in 1982.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: Two-part documentary series examining the years between 1977 and 1984 when three English football clubs - Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa - lifted the European Cup a record seven times. Featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers the break-up of Brian Clough's hugely successful Nottingham Forest, the re-emergence of Liverpool - who lifted their third and fourth European Cups in 1981 and 1984 - and the incredible story of Aston Villa, who upset all the odds to claim their one and only win in the competition in 1982.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: Two-part documentary series examining the years between 1977 and 1984 when three English football clubs - Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa - lifted the European Cup a record seven times. Featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers the break-up of Brian Clough's hugely successful Nottingham Forest, the re-emergence of Liverpool - who lifted their third and fourth European Cups in 1981 and 1984 - and the incredible story of Aston Villa, who upset all the odds to claim their one and only win in the competition in 1982.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: Two-part documentary series examining the years between 1977 and 1984 when three English football clubs - Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa - lifted the European Cup a record seven times. programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: Two-part documentary series examining the years between 1977 and 1984 when three English football clubs - Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa - lifted the European Cup a record seven times. Featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers the break-up of Brian Clough's hugely successful Nottingham Forest, the re-emergence of Liverpool - who lifted their third and fourth European Cups in 1981 and 1984 - and the incredible story of Aston Villa, who upset all the odds to claim their one and only win in the competition in 1982.

programme.title: Millionaire Hot Seat
programme.desc: Jeremy Clarkson hosts the exciting and fast-paced quiz where each episode sees six hopefuls compete for a one-million-pound prize - however, only one player can take their place in the Hot Seat at a time and answer multiple-choice questions to work their way up the Money Ladder. Unlike classic Millionaire, each question is against the clock and there is no room for indecision - if a player answers correctly, they remain in the Hot Seat and continue up the Money Ladder, but if they get a question wrong, they are eliminated, the Top Prize drops down, and the next player takes their place. Each player is given one Pass - a chance to pass the question on to the next player - but in doing so forfeit their place in the Hot Seat and risk not making it back there later on. Only one player will have a chance to win the top prize remaining on the ladder, and the player taking on that question must answer it correctly to take home the cash.

programme.title: When English Football Ruled Europe
programme.desc: Two-part documentary series examining the years between 1977 and 1984 when three English football clubs - Liverpool, Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa - lifted the European Cup a record seven times. Featuring interviews with the stars of the victorious teams, the series reveals the remarkable stories behind the triumphs and explains how some of the most colourful characters in the game mastered Europe's foremost club competition. This part covers the break-up of Brian Clough's hugely successful Nottingham Forest, the re-emergence of Liverpool - who lifted their third and fourth European Cups in 1981 and 1984 - and the incredible story of Aston Villa, who upset all the odds to claim their one and only win in the competition in 1982.
